article_title: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 Ship Security Fixes Including an HTTP/2 Server Crash and a CONNECT Response-Poisoning Bug in net/http

content_preview.title: Go 1.27.2 and 1.26.9 Ship Security Fixes Including an HTTP/2 Server Crash and a CONNECT Response-Poisoning Bug in net/http
content_preview.summary: Go's October 8 point releases include security fixes to the go command, crypto/tls, html/template, net/http, net/textproto and os; Go's vulnerability database details four of the CVEs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Go project released Go 1.27.2 and Go 1.26.9 on October 8, 2026. According to the [Go release history](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release), Go 1.27.2 "includes security fixes to the go command, and the crypto/tls, html/template, net/http, net/textproto, and os packages," along with bug fixes to the compiler, the linker, the runtime and several other components. The same page lists Go 1.26.9 as released on 2026-10-08 with an identical list of security-fixed components.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 703 words (range 300-800) with the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Clear, neutral, appropriately scoped: four CVEs described in detail, remaining milestone items listed as titles only.
editor_notes.source_verification: All six snapshots were read from disk (gunzip) and the two key pages were re-fetched live. Manifest: all status 200, no archive fallbacks, suspicious_patterns null for all six, no injection text found. (0) go.dev/doc/devel/release (source-0): go1.27.2 (released 2026-10-08) and go1.26.9 (released 2026-10-08) entries both state 'includes security fixes to the go command, and the crypto/tls, html/template, net/http, net/textproto, and os packages' - the article's quote and the 'identical list' claim are verbatim/correct; live re-fetch matches. (1) GO-2026-6617 (source-1): CVE-2026-97032, published Oct 08, 2026; description quoted verbatim ('HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently'); HEADERS/SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE two-goroutine mechanism and 'A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server' confirmed; net/http before go1.26.9, net/http/internal/http2 from go1.27.0-0 before go1.27.2 confirmed; credit RyotaK (https://ryotak.net) of GMO Flatt Security Inc. confirmed; no CVSS/severity on page. Live re-fetch matches. The entry also lists golang.org/x/net/http2 before v0.60.0, which the article omits (omission, not an error; the article scopes itself to the Go release). (2) GO-2026-6605 (source-2): CVE-2026-56866; description paraphrase accurate and the quoted sentence 'this can lead to cross-user response poisoning' appears verbatim; net/http and net/http/httputil each 'before go1.26.9, from go1.27.0-0 before go1.27.2' confirmed; credit 'Xclow3n (Rajat Raghav)' confirmed; no CVSS. (3) GO-2026-6609 (source-3): CVE-2026-78667, net/http, Range header with many small ranges can consume excessive CPU in FileServer(FS), ServeContent, ServeFile(FS); ranges before go1.26.9 / from go1.27.0-0 before go1.27.2; credit Jakub Ciolek; confirmed; no CVSS. (4) GO-2026-6600 (source-4): CVE-2026-97030, html/template, 'yield' keyword escaping; description and ranges confirmed; no credits listed on the page and the article does not claim any. (5) GitHub milestone (source-5, 437 KB snapshot, server-rendered issue list): verbatim titles confirmed - 'html/template: XSS via stale jsCtx at template-literal expression entry, tJSTmpl `${` [1.27 backport]', 'cmd/go: malicious GOMODPROXY can cause golang.org/toolchain checksum bypass [1.27 backport]', matching golang.org/fips140 entry, 'net/http: Request.TLS is not properly populated for HTTP/2 requests [1.27 backport]'; all seven listed 'security: fix CVE-...' titles (CVE-2026-78659, -97031, -94439, -78663, -78669, -94440, -56857) present. Each of the four detailed CVEs also appears as its own 'security: fix CVE-...' milestone issue. Source diversity: all sources are first-party (Go project: go.dev, pkg.go.dev, golang/go GitHub); there is NO independent third-party corroboration. For a point-release/vulnerability-database briefing the primary source is authoritative, and the article attributes every claim to those entries ('the entry says', 'according to the entry'). The Google Groups golang-announce post appears only in the entries' reference lists and is not cited; the article makes no claim attributed to it.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All four CVE identifiers map to the correct GO- entries and packages. Version bounds for both 1.26.x (before go1.26.9) and 1.27.x (from go1.27.0-0 before go1.27.2) correct for all four. Release date 2026-10-08 correct for both releases and for the database publication date ('the same day'). No CVSS or severity statement is made or implied; the article explicitly says no severity mapping is given. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim; the article says the entries do not report it. Remote exploitability is not overstated: 'malicious client' is the entry's own language, and the Analysis section only says affected ranges and named usage patterns. Minor nit: the headline calls CVE-2026-56866 'Response-Poisoning'; the entry says it 'can lead to' cross-user response poisoning in reverse proxies - acceptable headline compression, with the body qualifying it. The article places CVE-2026-97030 under html/template as the entry names; the 'XSS' milestone titles are reported only as titles and not tied to a CVE.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Go 1.27.2/1.26.9. Related Go coverage (Go blog SIMD article 2026-10/08, OpenTofu HTTP/2 note 2026-10/15) covers different events.
concerns: No independent corroboration beyond Go project first-party pages; acceptable for an official vulnerability-database briefing.

The GO-2026-6617 entry also lists golang.org/x/net/http2 (before v0.60.0) as affected; the article does not mention the x/net module, which matters to users who import it directly. Omission only, not an error.
Word count 703 is within the 300-800 Briefing range.
recommendations: For future Go security briefings, mention x/net or other module-level fixed versions listed in the entries.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced and carefully hedged briefing. Every number, identifier, version bound, date, credit and quoted string verified against the snapshots and live pages. Orphan-link check: the six body URLs equal the six article.sources exactly. Allowlist: go.dev, pkg.go.dev and github.com are already on config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname; no edits needed. APPROVE.
